messages:
Maria Gomez: quick summary — I ran a cross-benchmark comparing adaptive-kernel + heuristic-batching vs fixed-kernel + fixed-batching across streaming and non-streaming paths. attaching brief numbers and observations below.
Jamal Singh: nice, was this on replay harness or synth load?
Maria Gomez: replay harness with 24h production trace (sampled 10%) + synth Poisson overlay for tail. kept seed and concurrency the same. KV cache warmed for 30m before collecting metrics.
Li Chen: what were the kernel selection rules in 'adaptive'?
Maria Gomez: adaptive = runtime picks kernel by sequence-length histogram + current batch size; fallback to small-k for <64 tokens, fused-attn for long seqs. batching heuristic aggregates until latency budget or max_batch=64. config snippet:
```
{"kernel_policy":"adaptive","batching":"heuristic","max_batch":64,"latency_budget_ms":120}
```
Tia Brooks: and fixed setup?
Maria Gomez: fixed = force kernel=fused-attn, batch_size=32, no prefix caching changes. streaming path chunk_size=64 tokens for both. client read-loop poll interval left at 5ms.
Jamal Singh: raw numbers? p50/p95 p99 and tokens/sec pls
Maria Gomez: ok numbers (synth overlay + replay combined, avg over 30min):
- adaptive streaming: p50=32ms p95=210ms p99=480ms tokens/s=78k
- adaptive non-streaming: p50=40ms p95=260ms p99=610ms tokens/s=64k
- fixed streaming: p50=45ms p95=330ms p99=920ms tokens/s=52k
- fixed non-streaming: p50=55ms p95=380ms p99=1100ms tokens/s=48k
Li Chen: wow adaptive streaming looks much better at tail and throughput. did you isolate KV cache effects?
Maria Gomez: yes — ran ablation where KV cache disabled: adaptive streaming p95 jumped ~60ms, tokens/s dropped ~18%. KV cache hit-rate correlated with chunk alignment; misaligned client chunks -> lower KV hits.
Tia Brooks: chunking/backpressure specifics? any stalls in readloop?
Maria Gomez: saw short readloop stalls when client chunk size < kernel-preferred granularity (e.g., chunk=16). Adaptive kernel tried to coalesce but hit per-chunk scheduling overhead. backpressure manifested as increased queue depth and occasional kernel-switch churn.
Jamal Singh: did you try increasing client read-loop backoff or batching at proxy?
Maria Gomez: yes — bumping client poll to 10ms reduced churn but hurt latency p50 by ~6ms. better approach: proxy-level coalescing for small chunks (hold 2-3 chunks up to 20ms) — gave best tradeoff: p95 down ~30ms versus naive 5ms.
Li Chen: profiler artifacts? which hotspots?
Maria Gomez: cpu sampling showed most time in scheduler and kernel-selection path when churn high. GPU timelines showed many sub-64-token kernels underutilizing SMs. KV read stalls accounted for ~12% of end-to-end in worst cases.
perf-bot: perf-bench run 1867894321 completed: summary uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-perf/1867894321/crossbench-summary.json
Tia Brooks: any regression signals vs last stable?
Maria Gomez: compared to last stable (commit abc123): adaptive configs improved p95 by 22% for streaming, but introduced a regression for non-streaming p50 under tiny-batch corner cases (seen at very low concurrency). filing a follow-up perf issue.
Jamal Singh: sounds actionable — next steps?
Maria Gomez: 1) enable proxy-level coalescing for streaming experiments, 2) tune kernel threshold heuristics to avoid switching for sequences <24 tokens, 3) add KV cache alignment telemetry to production trace. I can open PRs for (1) and (2) and a perf ticket for (3).
Li Chen: add a small test in replay harness to vary client-chunk-size distribution (16/32/64) so we catch regressions in CI.
Maria Gomez: will do. thanks all, will post updated numbers once PRs land. :thumbsup:
